entries.title: Coverage diagnosis is a process, not a single tell
entries.summary: One coaching framework begins with game situation, then safety structure and secondary/blitz indicators. Super SAGE should treat pre-snap indicators probabilistically and confirm with post-snap behavior.
limitations: The cited checklist is a coaching framework, not a universal quarterback progression.

entries.title: Cover 6 / quarter-quarter-half family
entries.summary: USA Football coaching material identifies Cover 6 as a quarter-quarter-half coverage option. SAGE should model split-field coverage as potentially different rules to opposite sides rather than forcing one whole-field label.

entries.title: Tampa 2 changes underneath/deep-middle behavior
entries.summary: A documented offensive teaching example distinguishes Tampa 2 from conventional Cover 2 because the middle defender's depth can make the structure behave differently for route reads. SAGE should not treat all two-high Cover 2-family calls as identical.
limitations: This entry captures an offensive teaching perspective, not a complete Tampa 2 defensive manual.

entries.title: Post-snap coverage behavior should outrank static pre-snap shell labels
entries.summary: Because defenses can rotate/disguise and split rules by side, SAGE may gain predictive value from post-snap coverage classification and player-side assignment rather than pre-snap shell percentages alone.
